about: One finished video in the shape, length and size each place takes: 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9, with a crop that follows what moves, and a check of any file against a place's limits.

tools.name: reframe_video
tools.title: A video in each place's shape
makes: each place's version of a video
tools.asks: a video for TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube, X or LinkedIn: vertical, square or 4:5, or cut to a place's length or size
tools.description: Turns one finished video into the version each place takes, with ffmpeg on this machine: 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, 4:5 for the feeds, 1:1, and 16:9 for YouTube, X and LinkedIn. In each shot the crop follows what moves, not faces, and a shot whose action or words are wider than the crop is padded, shown whole on a blurred copy of itself. Each file is cut at a shot change to its place's length, kept under its size limit, set to the loudness asked for, given a cover beside it and checked against the limits the place publishes. FORMATS.md, which the result shows, lists every file with its checks; sheet.png, the picture to show first, draws each shape's window on every shot. A launch film's timeline or a demo's steps file beside the video gives its shots. To move a window, plan first and edit crop.json. For a look at the windows before anything renders, use plan_reframe instead.
tools.hostedDescription: Turns one finished video into the version each place takes: 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, 4:5 for the feeds, 1:1, and 16:9 for YouTube, X and LinkedIn. In each shot the crop follows what moves, not faces, and a shot whose action or words are wider than the crop is padded, shown whole on a blurred copy of itself. Each file is cut at a shot change to its place's length, kept under its size limit, set to the loudness asked for, given a cover beside it and checked against the limits the place publishes. FORMATS.md, which the result shows, lists every file with its checks; sheet.png, the picture to show first, draws each shape's window on every shot. A launch film's timeline or a demo's steps file beside the video, as in that job's own files, gives its shots. A window cannot be moved here. For a look at the windows before anything renders, use plan_reframe instead.

video.description: The finished video, any file ffmpeg reads, like film.mp4 from a launch film or demo.mp4 from a demo. The film.timeline.json or steps.json beside it, under its name, gives its shots.

for.description: The places, in one run at most {fact:reframekit.places_max}: any of tiktok ({fact:reframekit.size.tiktok}), reels ({fact:reframekit.size.reels}), shorts ({fact:reframekit.size.shorts}), youtube ({fact:reframekit.size.youtube}), x ({fact:reframekit.size.x}), linkedin ({fact:reframekit.size.linkedin}), feed ({fact:reframekit.size.feed}, for the 4:5 feeds), square ({fact:reframekit.size.square}), all (every one of them, the default), or a size like 1080x1350, even sides of {fact:reframekit.side_min} to {fact:reframekit.side_max} pixels from 1:4 to 4:1.

mode.description: follow crops each shot where what moves is, and pads a shot a crop would cut (default {default:reframe_video.mode}); center crops from the middle; pad shows every shot whole on a blurred copy or a color; fit keeps the picture's own shape and only fits each place's limits.

pad.description: What a padded shot sits on: blur (default, a blurred, darkened copy of itself), black, white, a color like #0f172a, or brand, the page background of the brand kit given as brand.

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder, brand.json or _brand.yml: padded shots then sit on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.
brand.hostedDescription: A brand kit an earlier job saved, as job:<job_id>/brand.json: padded shots then sit on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.

crop.description: A crop.json from plan_reframe or an earlier run, edited by hand: its windows are rendered as they are, and a shape it has none of is planned for its shots. It takes no cuts or steps, and no mode but fit.

cuts.description: Every shot change, in place of those found: seconds like 3.2,7.5, or a JSON file of seconds, of frames with their fps like {"fps": 30, "cuts": [96, 225]}, a launch film's film.timeline.json or a demo's steps.json.

steps.description: The steps.json of the demo this video is, when it is not beside the video under its name: it gives the pages, the page box and each click.

seconds.description: Keep at most this long in each place's video, cut at a shot change: seconds like "30", or "1:30".

trim.description: Set to false never to cut a file to its place's length, for an account a place allows more, like TikTok's 10 minutes; FORMATS.md then says the file is over.

lufs.description: The loudness of every file in LUFS (default {default:reframe_video.lufs}).

fps.description: The files' frame rate, like 30 or 29.97 (default: the video's own, within what the places take).

cover.description: The moment each place's cover shows, in seconds like "4.5" or as "0:04.5" (default: picked).

done: Show {file:sheet.png} to the user before the files go out: the crop follows what moves, not faces, so check that each window holds the person, the product and the words.
FORMATS.md below says which files passed their place's limits and what was cut to length; hand each file over for its place with its cover beside it.
To move a window, edit {file:crop.json} and call reframe_video again with crop {file:crop.json}, the same video and the same places.

Give the user the {name:sheet.png} link from the list below before the files go out: the crop follows what moves, not faces, so they should check that each window holds the person, the product and the words.
FORMATS.md below says which files passed their place's limits and what was cut to length; give the user each file's own link from the list below, with its cover.

tools.name: plan_reframe
tools.title: Plan each place's crop
tools.asks: to see a video's crop for each place before it renders
tools.description: Plans what reframe_video renders, without rendering: finds the shots of a finished video and, for each place's shape, a window that follows what moves in each shot, or a padded shot where a crop would cut too much. Writes crop.json, every shot with its window for each shape, sheet.png, each shape's window drawn on every shot's frames (a solid outline for a crop, a dashed one for a padded shot), with more shots in sheet-2.png and on, and FORMATS.md, which the result shows with the command that renders the plan. Look at the sheet, move a window that misses in crop.json, then give that crop.json to reframe_video as crop. A plan in a folder of an earlier render keeps its files. For the files themselves in one job, use reframe_video instead.
tools.hostedDescription: Plans what reframe_video renders, without rendering: finds the shots of a finished video and, for each place's shape, a window that follows what moves in each shot, or a padded shot where a crop would cut too much. Writes crop.json, every shot with its window for each shape, sheet.png, each shape's window drawn on every shot's frames (a solid outline for a crop, a dashed one for a padded shot), with more shots in sheet-2.png and on, and FORMATS.md, which the result shows. A crop.json cannot be changed here, so reframe_video given the same video and places renders the windows as this plan has them. For the files themselves in one job, use reframe_video instead.

video.description: The finished video, any file ffmpeg reads, like film.mp4 from a launch film or demo.mp4 from a demo. The film.timeline.json or steps.json beside it, under its name, gives its shots.

for.description: The places to plan for, in one run at most {fact:reframekit.places_max}: any of tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube, x, linkedin, feed, square, all (the default) or a size like 1080x1350, as reframe_video takes them.

mode.description: follow crops each shot where what moves is, and pads a shot a crop would cut (default {default:plan_reframe.mode}); center crops from the middle; pad shows every shot whole; fit keeps the picture's own shape.

pad.description: What a padded shot sits on: blur (default), black, white, a color like #0f172a, or brand, which needs brand. The render command the plan gives carries it.

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder, brand.json or _brand.yml, for padded shots on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.
brand.hostedDescription: A brand kit an earlier job saved, as job:<job_id>/brand.json, for padded shots on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.

crop.description: An edited crop.json whose shapes to keep: the plan adds the windows of a place whose shape it has none of. It takes no cuts or steps, and no mode but fit.

cuts.description: Every shot change, in place of those found: seconds like 3.2,7.5, or a JSON file of seconds, of frames with their fps, a launch film's film.timeline.json or a demo's steps.json.

steps.description: The steps.json of the demo this video is, when it is not beside the video under its name.

seconds.description: Keep at most this long in each place's video, cut at a shot change: seconds like "30", or "1:30". The render command the plan gives carries it.

trim.description: Set to false never to cut a file to its place's length. The render command the plan gives carries it.

lufs.description: The loudness the files will have in LUFS (default {default:plan_reframe.lufs}), for the render command the plan gives.

fps.description: The files' frame rate (default: the video's own), for the render command the plan gives.

cover.description: The moment each place's cover shows, in seconds like "4.5" (default: picked).

done: Look at {file:sheet.png}, or give the user its path, and check that each window holds the person, the product and the words.
Move a window that misses in {file:crop.json}, then call reframe_video with crop {file:crop.json}, the same video and the same places.
Give the user the {name:sheet.png} link from the list below, to check that each window holds the person, the product and the words.
A crop.json cannot be changed here: when the windows are right, call reframe_video with the same video and places, which renders them as planned.

tools.name: check_place_limits
tools.title: Check videos against each place's limits
makes: a check of a video against each place's limits
tools.asks: a video checked against a place's limits, or burned captions against a phone app's safe area
tools.description: Measures finished MP4 files against each place's published limits without changing them: shape, size, frame rate, length, file size, codecs, and whether the MP4 is whole and laid out as Instagram and YouTube ask. Give it a folder reframe_video made, its formats.json, or one MP4 with the places in for. With captions, the ASS, SRT or WebVTT file burned into the video, it checks their timing, and an ASS file's text against each 9:16 place's safe area. It writes CHECK.md, which the result shows, and check.json. A failed check is a normal result, with what failed and the limit's source. It does not say whether a video may be posted. For loudness, black, still and silent stretches, use check_video instead.

target.description: What to check: a folder reframe_video made, its formats.json, or one MP4, like captioned.mp4.

for.description: The places to check a lone MP4 against, any of tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube, x, linkedin, feed and square (default: the places of its shape); with a folder, only these.

captions.description: The ASS, SRT or WebVTT file of the captions burned into the video: its timing is checked, and an ASS file's text against each 9:16 place's safe area. caption_video writes captions.ass beside its captioned.mp4.

passed: Tell the user each file passed its place's limits, with any warning CHECK.md below gives, and that the limits are what each place published when the kit read them.
check_failed: Read which file failed which limit in CHECK.md below, and tell the user.
A file too long, too large or of the wrong shape for its place comes out within its limits from reframe_video.
Captions in a 9:16 place's margins keep clear of every 9:16 place once caption_video has tiktok, reels and shorts in for, and position middle moves them higher.
